# 2.1.5 Dot Product

Dot Product, also called the **inner product**, is a widely used operation in linear algebra. Similar to elementwise operations, the dot product requires both vectors (usually column vectors) to be of the same length.

\

**Definition 2.1.5** (Dot Product). \ The **dot product** of two vectors $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the sum of the products of their corresponding elements. It is defined as:
$$
\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = \sum_{i=1}^{n} u_i v_i = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2 + \cdots + u_n v_n = \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{v}
$$
where $\mathbf{u}^T$ is the transpose of the column vector $\mathbf{u}$.

\
\

**Example 2.1.5**
$$
\mathbf{u} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad
\mathbf{v} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Then,
$$
\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 2 \cdot 1 + 3 \cdot 5 + 4 \cdot 7 = 2 + 15 + 28 = 45 \in \mathbb{R}
$$

So, the result of the dot product is a **scalar**.
